items.reason: The distinct Burns Paiute Tribal government is confirmed by its own homepage and federal directory. Its account of Wadatika ancestry does not encompass all Northern Paiute peoples.
The strategic plan attributes the 1878 account to the Tribe. Exact dates within the year remain unspecified.
The Tribe’s About BPT account describes language continuity outside school during the 1920s.
Sections 1 and 2 establish the reservation in trust. The statute and the Tribe’s accounts have different scopes. The fact omits acreage and recognition chronology.
The Tribal Council resolution expressly recognizes a language emergency, calls for a language plan, and certifies adoption on February 2, 2017.
